Major findings (diet-depression relation: Adequate intake of fruits and vegetables was associated with a significant reduction in the risk of depressive symptoms.

Higher intake of carbohydrates and fat was significantly associated with more depressive symptoms. A significant negative association was found between magnesium intake and depressive symptoms when controlling for total energy intake.

A higher diet quality, including fruits available at home, daily servings of fruits and vegetables, eating fruits after school, and consuming fruit drinks on school days, was significantly associated with lower scores of depressive symptoms at ages 15.6 and 17.4.
